title: Java Write to Files
learningObjectives: Write text to a file with FileWriter.
Use try-with-resources to close a writer reliably.
Append content without replacing existing content.
Understand character encoding and IOException concerns.
Verify written text by reading it back.

understand.concept: Java's FileWriter writes character data to a file. Opening it in the default mode replaces existing content; the constructor with append=true adds content to the end. Writers should be closed so buffered characters are flushed. Try-with-resources closes the writer automatically, including when an exception occurs. For explicit character encodings in modern applications, prefer Files.newBufferedWriter with a StandardCharsets value.
understand.whyItMatters: File handling allows a Java application to persist, retrieve and manage information beyond the lifetime of a single run.
understand.analogy: Think of a path as a labeled address to a storage location; the address and the data stored there are different things.
understand.analogyLimit: A path is not a guarantee that the target exists or that the program has permission to access it.

explain.narrative: Import java.io.FileWriter and java.io.IOException. Create a writer in try-with-resources, call write, and let the resource close at the end of the block. Use new FileWriter(path, true) when appending. FileWriter uses the platform default charset, so use java.nio.file.Files.newBufferedWriter and StandardCharsets.UTF_8 when a predictable encoding is required.

examples.title: Write text
examples.explanation: write sends characters to the writer, and closing it flushes them before reading the file.

examples.title: Append text
examples.explanation: The append constructor preserves existing content and writes new characters at the end.

examples.title: Write multiple lines
examples.explanation: A newline character separates the two written lines in the file.

examples.title: Write UTF-8 explicitly
examples.explanation: Files.newBufferedWriter accepts an explicit charset for predictable text encoding.

examples.title: Replace existing content
examples.explanation: The one-argument FileWriter constructor truncates an existing file before writing.

practise.guidedTask: Create a small Java program that demonstrates java write to files. Predict each result, then compile and run it with JDK 21.
practise.independentTask: Build a practical Java file-handling utility related to java write to files. Include at least two test cases, expected outputs, and an explanation of failure handling and path safety.
hints: Start with a Path or File that points to a controlled test location.
Use try-with-resources for streams and writers, and handle IOException where the API declares it.
Test both the normal case and an edge case such as a missing path or existing target.
practise.challenge: Extend one java write to files example to handle a realistic file-system edge case safely and explain the API behaviour.
